email.subject: MV BRYONY HEAD - Port report Samarinda - crane breakdown
email.body:
Port report, Samarinda, 21 Jan 2025.

Crane No. 3 hydraulic pump failed at 0230 UTC and loading at hold 3 stopped. Ship's engineers changed the pump; the crane was back in service and loading at hold 3 resumed at 1145 UTC. The other three cranes worked throughout. Stevedores at hold 3 stood by.

Estimated completion of loading now 23 Jan 0600 UTC.

Master MV BRYONY HEAD

output.off_hire_clause: Off hire (fictional, modelled on NYPE 1993 clause 17): in the event of loss of time from breakdown of, or damage to, hull, machinery or equipment, or any other similar cause preventing the full working of the vessel, the payment of hire shall cease for the time thereby lost. All bunkers used by the vessel while off hire shall be for the owners' account. Rider (fictional): in the event of a breakdown of the vessel's cargo cranes, hire shall be reduced pro rata for the time lost, in the proportion that the number of cranes out of use bears to the total number of cranes.
output.war_risks_clause: War risks (fictional, modelled on BIMCO CONWARTIME 2013): the vessel shall not be obliged to proceed through any area where, in the reasonable judgement of the Master and/or the owners, she may be exposed to war risks. If the owners so decide, the charterers shall give other orders, and the vessel shall proceed by an alternative route. Extra time and bunkers on that route are for the charterers' account.

summary: Voyage Agent reports: The Master reports that Crane No. 3 failed on 21 Jan 2025 from 0230 UTC to 1145 UTC, during which loading at hold 3 stopped while the other three cranes continued to work. According to the CP terms...

result.result: The Master reports that Crane No. 3 failed on 21 Jan 2025 from 0230 UTC to 1145 UTC, during which loading at hold 3 stopped while the other three cranes continued to work. According to the CP terms' off-hire rider, hire should be reduced pro rata for the time lost in proportion to the cranes out of use. The simulated hire statement shows that for this 9.25-hour period with 1 of 4 cranes out of use (25% share), the hire deduction would be 1,156.25 USD. The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire pro rata and notify the owner. If agreed, the following would follow: (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period with one crane out of use, and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management providing the period, the crane involved, and the reason. I recommend that nothing be sent until the operator answers.
